summary:
Approved to proceed, with the eleven "fix" items below applied in the same commit as the code. The decision itself is right and I confirmed its two load-bearing claims myself: nothing in production matches `GateError` by class (only the definition at semantic_interpretation.py:849 and the raise at :903 exist; the only class matches are §15.5's vacuous `except GateError: raise` and two tests), and `add_note` genuinely reaches Isabelle — `traceback.format_exception` renders `__notes__`, `Isabelle_RPC_Host/rpc.py:344-347` forwards that whole string, and `Semantic_Store.extract_user_error` (semantic_store.ML:1435-1440) finds no marker in it, so the note plus the full chain is printed. Routing the D11 correction write into the run's task group also genuinely dissolves F2 rather than patching it: `on_answer` stops being able to raise for a store reason.

Four things must change before the sketch becomes code. (1) The seam: `on_answer` must not call `_spawn` directly. `start_gate` is the only seam the driver tests override (test_interpretation_driver.py:52, :243) and §15.10 prescribes it; bypassing it makes 20 tests in three modules fail on `_spawn`'s `assert self.task_group is not None`, and makes the one test that does own a group (:257-279) run the production `_gate` against the developer's real cache. Collapse `start_gate`/`_spawn` into ONE index-bearing seam `start_write(idx, write)` taking the coroutine function, so a single stub override keeps LMDB out of both branches. (2) The traceback: I measured that `raise leaves[0] from leaves[0].__cause__` inside `except ExceptionGroup` overwrites the leaf's `__context__` with the group and then suppresses it — and with `GateError` gone that context is the store failure's only remaining lead. It is a live path: `put_interpretation` → `invalidate_vectors` → `_get_lmdb_env` → `_rebuild_corrupt_store`'s `os.rename` (semantic_embedding.py:1053-1079) raises an OSError whose `__context__` is the lmdb corruption error and whose `__cause__` is None. Raising the leaf AFTER the except block has been left drops the group structurally, keeps cause and context, needs no `from` at all, and retires §5.4's `raise leaves[0] from None` sentence instead of replacing it with a second trick (measured). (3) The amendment list is short by eleven plan passages, and the worst omission is §15.5's `_gate` block: its `finally: task.gate_finished()` beside `_finishing`'s own decrement makes the counter go negative, `not -1` is False, and the loop parks forever in `wait_for_progress()` — byte-for-byte F3's measured hang. (4) The sketch's `match self.state[idx]` does not compile (`case _DONE` is a capture pattern; CPython 3.12.3 rejects it with "name capture '_DONE' makes remaining patterns unreachable"): keep today's if-chain.

Naming: all three lenses are right that `gates_running` would count things §0 defines as not gates. One counter, renamed `writes_running`, with one new glossary row defining "write task"; `tasks_running` is refused because "task" already means `AgentTask` throughout this file.

One thing to put in front of the user (item 14, the only "discuss-with-user"): this decision makes a failed correction LOUD, but it does not make it recoverable. Once the entity's gate has written its record with the current digest, the next scan finds it fresh and never re-asks — so the correction is gone even though the run failed and the theory is unmarked. That is worth one sentence in §6.4 and worth the user hearing, because it is the premise their decision was reasoning about.

items.title: `on_answer` bypasses `start_gate`, the seam §15.10 prescribes (failure-semantics F1)
items.reasoning: Stands, and it is the same defect as the plan-consistency lens's first finding; I rule them together and adopt the single-seam remedy. Verified on disk: `_RecordingTask.start_gate` (archive/tests/test_interpretation_driver.py:52-53) is the module's entire no-LMDB substitute, `_FailingGateTask.start_gate` (:243-254) is the second override, `_make_task` is imported by test_interpretation_mcp_server.py and test_interpretation_codex.py as well, and none of the 20 tests that drive `_run(task, script)` ever sets `task.task_group`. With `on_answer` calling `_spawn`, every one of them dies on `assert self.task_group is not None` inside the real answer-tool handler, and `test_a_gate_failure_ends_the_run_as_its_own_exception` (:257-279), which DOES set `task.task_group = tg`, would run the production `_gate` for entries 0 and 2 — a real `Semantic_DB.gate_write()` of fabricated `b"\x00"*31`-suffixed keys into the developer's ~/.cache store, which F6's ruling explicitly warns against for step 3. I reject the two-method variant (`start_gate` + `start_correction`) proposed here in favour of one seam: with two methods a stub that overrides only `start_gate` still lets a correction reach the group (today it reaches real LMDB, tomorrow an assert), so the trap survives in a new shape. One seam makes it unstateable.
items.fix:
Delete `_spawn` and `start_gate`; put ONE seam on `AgentTask` beside the counter:

    def start_write(self, idx: int, write) -> None:
        """Run one entity's store write as a task of the run's group: counted,
        so the queue loop waits for it; its failure fails the run.  THE one
        place the counter moves."""
        assert self.task_group is not None, "interpret_file owns the run's task group"
        self.writes_running += 1
        coro = write(self, idx)
        try:
            t = self.task_group.create_task(coro)
        except BaseException:
            coro.close(); self._write_finished(); raise
        t.add_done_callback(lambda _t: self._write_finished())

`on_answer` then reads `self.start_write(idx, _correct)` in the `_DONE` branch and `self.start_write(idx, _gate)` in the fall-through. `_RecordingTask` overrides `start_write(self, idx, write)` once (records `(idx, self.results[idx])`, marks `_DONE`) and covers both branches with no task group and no LMDB; `_FailingGateTask` (and F7's `_SlowGateTask`) call `super().start_write(idx, <its own write>)` instead of hand-rolling the counter. Taking the coroutine FUNCTION, not a coroutine object, is what lets a stub decline to run it without a never-awaited warning.

items.title: The amendment list omits §15.5's `_gate` block: `except GateError: raise` and a second `gate_finished()` (failure-semantics F2)
items.reasoning: Stands. Grep confirms seven `GateError` mentions in the plan (lines 325, 616, 762, 816, 1009, 1071, 1291); the note's list covers only 325, 762, 816, 1071 and §15.3. Line 1009 is inside §15.5's `_gate` code block — the block step 4/5 transcribes — and three lines below it sits `finally: task.gate_finished()` (line 1012, mirrored today at semantic_interpretation.py:913-916). Left in place beside the wrapper's own decrement, each write does one increment and two decrements; after N writes the counter is -N, `_run_agent`'s `if not task.gates_running: break` (:995) never fires because `not -1` is False (I ran it), and with the queue empty the loop parks in `wait_for_progress()` on an event only `enqueue` or a decrement can set. That is F3's measured permanent park, with `interpret_file` never returning and the Isabelle RPC call never completing. The `except GateError: raise` arm is vacuous today (the try has no `except Exception`), but it names a class this change deletes.
items.fix: Add §15.5's `_gate` block to the amendment list and, in it, delete `except asyncio.CancelledError: raise`, `except GateError: raise` and `finally: task.gate_finished()` — with the counter paired by `start_write`, `_gate` needs no `try` at all and shrinks to the straight-line body. State the invariant once, in §5.4 and in `start_write`'s docstring: the counter is moved by `start_write` alone; no coroutine submitted to the group touches it.

items.title: `_finishing`'s `finally` is skipped when its task is cancelled before its first step (failure-semantics F3)
items.reasoning: Stands at minor, on exactly F4's accepted standing (the counter is the loop's only termination signal and a violated counter's symptom is a hang), and I reproduced it inside a real TaskGroup rather than in isolation: a gate that fails at its first step aborts the group; a correction spawned in that window — ordinary agent behaviour, since the SDK dispatches each `answer` call in its own detached task and the tool's own 'Batch complete … correct them now' reply invites a correction — is created and then cancelled before it ever runs, so `_finishing`'s `try` is never entered. Measured: counter stranded at 1 plus a `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'correction' was never awaited`; the same scenario with a done callback ends at 0 with no warning. Like F4 the strand is unobservable today (the group is already aborting and `interpret_file` is about to raise), which is why it is minor and not major — but the remedy deletes a helper rather than adding one, so there is no reason to keep the weaker shape.
items.fix: Fold it into `start_write` as shown in item 1: pair the decrement to the task object with `t.add_done_callback(lambda _t: self._write_finished())`, which fires for every terminal state including a pre-start cancellation, and `coro.close()` on the `create_task`-raises edge. `_finishing` disappears. The decrement is then deferred by one `call_soon` relative to the task's completion, which is safe in the only direction that matters — the loop can never observe zero early — and `_write_finished` still sets `_progress` in the same callback, so a parked loop wakes on an already-decremented counter (measured).

items.title: The sketch's `match self.state[idx]` does not compile (elegance F1)
items.reasoning: Stands on the compile claim, which I reproduced verbatim on this interpreter: the three-case `match` is rejected with `SyntaxError: name capture '_DONE' makes remaining patterns unreachable`, because `_DONE` is an undotted name and therefore a capture pattern (the constants are `_NOT_ENROLLED, _QUEUED, _SENT, _GATING, _DONE = range(5)` at semantic_interpretation.py:303). A SyntaxError is self-revealing — the module fails to import and every test goes red — so this is major, not a blocker: it cannot ship silently. I reject the finding's suggested remedy: converting the five states to an `enum.IntEnum` changes a §15.1 row that is not otherwise being touched, rewrites ~40 comparison sites, and buys no failure. I also reject the sub-point that the fall-through must enumerate `QUEUED | SENT` rather than accept a default: `_NOT_ENROLLED` is refused by the answer tool at :739-742 two frames up, and 'a regression in that guard would…' is a hypothetical with no failure.
items.fix:
Keep today's if-chain in `on_answer` (semantic_interpretation.py:576-588), with the results assignment hoisted above it so every branch — including the correction — reads the newest text:

    self.results[idx] = text
    if self.state[idx] == _DONE:            # D11 on a written entity
        self.start_write(idx, _correct); return
    if self.state[idx] == _GATING:          # the gate writes the newest text
        return
    self.state[idx] = _GATING
    self.start_write(idx, _gate)

Write that shape into §15.3 in place of the `match` sketch.

items.title: Deleting `GateError` while keeping `raise leaves[0] from leaves[0].__cause__` destroys the store exception's own `__context__` (elegance F2)
items.reasoning: Stands, and it is the sharpest finding of the three lenses: the change's stated motivation is that 'a store failure is exactly the case where the traceback IS the lead', and F1's approved fix defeats that motivation once the wrapper is gone. Measured on this interpreter with a leaf shaped exactly like the live path: re-raising inside `except ExceptionGroup` sets `__context__` to the group (Python sets it on every raise), and `from leaf.__cause__` — which is `from None` for a native store exception — then suppresses it, so the leaf's original chain is clobbered and then hidden; the ValueError that was the actual lead does not appear anywhere in the output. The live path is in the tree and is documented as propagating: `put_interpretation` invalidates vectors first (semantics.py:990), `invalidate_vectors_in_store` opens through `_get_lmdb_env` ('open failures RAISE', semantic_embedding.py:1171), and its corruption arm calls `_rebuild_corrupt_store`, whose `os.rename` runs inside `except _CORRUPTION_ERRORS as e:` — so an OSError from the rename reaches `_write` with `__cause__ = None` and `__context__` = the corruption error. Raising outside the handler is strictly better and I measured all three properties at once: the group never appears (no `    | ` gutter), the leaf's cause and context both survive and render, the note still prints, and a marked `FatalAgentError` leaf still yields exactly its own message through `extract_user_error`.
items.fix:
Make the helper a selector and raise at the call site. Rename `_unwrap_gate_failures(eg) -> NoReturn` to `_first_failure(eg) -> BaseException`: flatten, drop `CancelledError` leaves, log `failures[1:]`, return `failures[0]`, or return `eg` unchanged when nothing but cancellations is left. In `interpret_file` (semantic_interpretation.py:1409-1415):

    failure: BaseException | None = None
    try:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
            task.task_group = tg
            await _run_agent(make_driver, task)
    except ExceptionGroup as eg:
        failure = _first_failure(eg)
    if failure is not None:
        raise failure

No `from`, no `__suppress_context__` mutation. §5.4's `raise leaves[0] from None` sentence is retired rather than corrected (this supersedes F1's one-token fix, which was right for the code it ruled on). In archive/tests/test_interpretation_driver.py:278 replace `assert e.value.__suppress_context__` (now False, and it never asserted what its comment claimed) with `assert not isinstance(e.value.__context__, BaseExceptionGroup)`, and add a case pinning that a leaf raised with its own `__context__` still shows it.

items.title: The counter, its mutators and the spawner live in different classes, and `gates_running` names something §0 says is not a gate (elegance F3)
items.reasoning: Stands, downgraded from major: there is no runtime failure today, and the finding's own evidence (`_FailingGateTask` hand-rolling `gate_started()` + `create_task`) is a test hazard, not a production one. But the project's rules weigh elegance as heavily as correctness and prefer a shape that makes an invariant unviolatable, and this change's stated point is 'one place that couples the counter to the task' — which the sketch does not deliver while the counter and its two public mutators sit on `AgentTask` and the group and spawner sit on `InterpretationTask`. Putting all four on `AgentTask` is also the smaller, more consistent edit: §15.2 already puts the whole queue machinery (`state`, `_queue`, `batch`, `_progress`) on the base even though a `JudgeTask` uses none of it. The naming half I settle under open question 1 (rename to `writes_running`).
items.fix: Move `task_group` to `AgentTask.__init__` (`self.task_group: asyncio.TaskGroup | None = None`) beside `self.writes_running = 0` and `self._progress`; add `start_write` (item 1) and a private `_write_finished` there; delete the public `gate_started` / `gate_finished`. `interpret_file` keeps setting `task.task_group = tg`. `_run_agent` reads `task.writes_running` (:995) and logs '(%d writes running)' (:999). Rebuild `_FailingGateTask` on `start_write` so no test hand-rolls the pair either.

items.title: `_noting(e: Entry)` bakes one sentence, but §5.4 step 6's write is a dependent's snapshot raise (elegance F4 = plan-consistency F5)
items.reasoning: Stands; both lenses raise it and they are right. §5.4's Failures paragraph puts step 6 on the same channel as step 5 ('Step 5's or step 6's failure…'), and §15.5's `_propagate` writes `update_gate_fields(uk_j, …)` for a DEPENDENT j inside its own `gate_write`. With the wrapper class gone, the note is the only text carrying the entity's identity, so a single baked 'while writing the interpretation of {e.name}' would send the operator after an interpretation write that never happened, on an entity that was not the one that failed. Catching `Exception` rather than `BaseException` is right for the same reason `_write` catches `Exception` today (:902): a cancellation delivered inside a future gate must not be annotated with a write it did not perform.
items.fix: Give the context manager the sentence, not the Entry, and name it for what it does: `_note_on_failure(note: str)`, `except Exception as exc: exc.add_note(note); raise`. Call sites: `with _note_on_failure(f"while writing the interpretation of {e.name}")` around `_write`'s `gate_write` block and around `_correct`'s `update_interpretation`; `with _note_on_failure(f"while raising the interpreted_at snapshot of {name_j}")` around `_propagate`'s write when step 5 lands. Put both note texts into the amended §5.4 Failures paragraph so the wordings are reviewable in one place, as the failure wordings already are.

items.title: "Every database write of a run shares one failure channel" overclaims (elegance F5)
items.reasoning: The wording half stands and is worth one careful sentence, because REPORT.md's proposal text (line 113) is what will be copied into §5.4 and §13 and it says 'every database write of a run shares one failure channel' and 'the blocking LMDB write leaves the event loop'. Both are false: the drivers' per-turn `write_cost` flush, the scan's phase-1 bumps and §5.3.2's `update_expr` refresh all write outside the group, and the correction write does not leave the loop — it leaves the tool handler and runs on the same loop thread one task later. The second half of the finding — that a `write_cost` failure inside a judge session is swallowed into a CHANGED verdict — is real but is not a defect to fix here: CHANGED is D2's conservative answer, and the same broken store fails the gate's own write moments later, which does fail the run. Do not widen the scope of this step to chase it.
items.fix: In the §5.4 and §13 amendments claim only what holds: 'every write of an interpretation — the gate's (§5.4 step 5), the snapshot raise (step 6) and D11's correction — is a task of the run's task group, so a failed one fails the run. The other writes of a run stay outside it: the drivers' per-turn `write_cost` flush, the scan's phase-1 bumps and §5.3.2's statement refresh.' Do not copy 'the blocking LMDB write leaves the event loop'.

items.title: The sketch bypasses `start_gate`, duplicating it as `_spawn` (plan-consistency F1)
items.reasoning: Same defect as item 1, and this lens's remedy is the one I adopt: one index-bearing seam taking the coroutine function, so `_RecordingTask` keeps LMDB and the task group out of BOTH branches with a single override and F8's correction test can live in the driver module with no store-backed fixture. Two identical spawn helpers, one of them dead, would also be the copy-paste the project rules forbid. I take only one thing off this item: `start_write` belongs on `AgentTask` beside the counter (item 6), not on `InterpretationTask`.
items.fix: As item 1. §15.10's sentence changes only `start_gate` → `start_write`; the stub's body ('records `(idx, results[idx])` and marks the entry `_DONE`, no LMDB, no task group') is unchanged.

items.title: The change is not confined to the five plan passages the note lists (plan-consistency F2)
items.reasoning: Stands; I checked all eight named passages and every one is falsified by the change, and grep confirms three `GateError` plan lines outside the note's list (616 in §10, 1009 in §15.5, 1291 in §15.10). Together with item 2's §15.5 `_gate` block that is eleven passages, not five. Leaving any of them makes plan and code disagree the moment the step lands, and §15 is 'the implementation blueprint the implementer follows', so a stale sentence there is not cosmetic — item 2 shows one of them producing a hang. The two on-disk tests that match `GateError` by class and assert `"T.c1" in str(e.value)` (test_interpretation_driver.py:250, :275-276, :283-286) must be rewritten in the same commit: with the wrapper gone the entity name lives only in `__notes__`, so the assertion moves to `"".join(traceback.format_exception(e.value))`.
items.fix: Extend the amendment list to: §5.3 Termination; §5.4 opening and Corrections (D11); §15.2's `AgentTask` block; §15.4's loop pseudocode and its completeness-certificate sentence; §15.5's `_gate` block, `_write` sentence and `_propagate`; §15.10 twice (the `_RecordingTask` sentence and the '`GateError` fails the run' cross-reference); §10's test bullet; §11's restated completeness comment; §0 (new glossary row); §6.4 (crash shape iii, item 14). Exact wordings are in plan_edits. For the certificate, state the strengthening explicitly rather than leaving it implicit: it now also certifies that every accepted D11 correction is on disk.

items.title: §15.11's "After step 3: behaviour equals today's" acceptance bullet no longer holds (plan-consistency F3)
items.reasoning: Stands. That bullet is the sentence the previous judge used to rule F2 major ('SCOPE's acceptance for this step is that the observable behaviour must equal today's'), so leaving it as written lets one sentence be read two ways and leaves the step with a self-contradictory acceptance criterion. The divergence is deliberate and is the user's own decision of 2026-09-08, so recording it is transcription, not a new decision — it needs no further approval, but it must be written down as a named exception rather than left implicit. The second, smaller divergence the finding notes is real too and costs one clause: even on success the correction's write is no longer synchronous with the tool reply; it lands at the handler's next await (`await _report(...)`), still before the reply reaches the agent.
items.fix: Rewrite the bullet's tail and record the decision in the plan's status paragraph beside the other 2026-09-08 approvals; wording in plan_edits.

items.title: `gates_running` would count things the glossary says are not gates (plan-consistency F4)
items.reasoning: Stands; this is open question 1 and all three lenses converge. §0 defines the gate as 'the decision, after a tracked entity has been re-interpreted, whether its meaning changed', and §5.4's Corrections paragraph says of a correction that 'the verdict stands' — it makes no decision and touches no gate field. Counting it in `gates_running`, starting it with `gate_started()`, and wording §5.3's Termination as 'every gate has finished' would make the glossary term false in the code, which is precisely what the project's one-term-per-concept rule exists to prevent. One counter is right: the loop's condition genuinely is 'no task of this run is outstanding', and two counters would make the break condition a conjunction a later author can get half-right. I refuse the elegance lens's `tasks_running` variant: 'task' already means `AgentTask` everywhere in this file (`_run_agent(make_driver, task)`, `task.task_group`), so `task.tasks_running` would give one word two meanings — the same rule, violated the other way. §15's preamble licenses a reviewer to change a name, so this does not go to the user.
items.fix: `gates_running` → `writes_running`; `gate_started`/`gate_finished` → the increment inside `start_write` and a private `_write_finished`; `start_gate` → `start_write`. Sites: semantic_interpretation.py:439-443, :568-571, :913-916, :995, :999; archive/tests/test_interpretation_driver.py:52, :243-254, :278 and the `gates_running` assertions; plan §0 (new row), §5.3, §5.4, §15.2, §15.3, §15.4, §11.

items.title: One `_noting(e)` text cannot serve both producers (plan-consistency F5)
items.reasoning: Same finding as item 7, independently reached; ruled there. Both lenses also agree on `except Exception` rather than `BaseException`, which matches `_write`'s deliberate exclusion of cancellation at semantic_interpretation.py:902.

items.title: ADDED BY THE JUDGE — this decision makes a failed correction loud, but it does not make it recoverable
items.reasoning: None of the three lenses states this plainly and the plan-consistency lens comes closest (it asks for a 'crash shape (iii)'), but the consequence is sharper than 'a widened window'. §6.4 lists two crash shapes and calls both recoverable because 'the next scan re-lists the entity by the very criterion that enrolled it'. A correction is not one of them. By the time a correction can be submitted the entity is `_DONE`, i.e. its record already carries the current `semantic_digest` and `deps` — so under §0's own definition of local staleness the next scan finds it FRESH and never re-asks it, whether the correction write failed, or the run died between the tool call and the write. The correction is lost permanently; what the user's decision buys is that the loss is loud (the run raises, the theory is not marked, the operator sees the store failure) instead of silent. That is a real improvement over today and I am not disputing the decision — but the user decided this while reasoning about a correction being lost, so they should hear that it is still lost, in case they would rather D11 also re-enrolled the entity (which would be a change to D11 and therefore theirs alone).
items.fix: Add crash shape (iii) to §6.4 (wording in plan_edits) and put one line in front of the user: 'a correction whose write does not commit is lost even though the run now fails — the entity's record is fresh by the scan's criteria, so the next run does not re-ask it. Do you want it left that way, or should D11 re-enrol the entity?' Do not implement any re-enrolment unless the user asks: it would change D11.

open_questions_settled:
**1. One counter for gates AND correction writes, or a broader name?**

One counter, renamed. Keep one, because the loop's exit condition really is the single fact "no task of this run is still outstanding"; splitting it in two would turn `_run_agent`'s break into a conjunction a later author can get half-right, for no benefit. But the name must change: §0 defines the gate as the CHANGED/UNCHANGED decision and §5.4 says of a correction that "the verdict stands", so `gates_running`, `gate_started` and §5.3's "every gate has finished" would all say "gate" for something the glossary says is not one. Rename to `writes_running` / (private) `_write_finished` / `start_write`, and define the union once in §0 rather than overloading a defined term: "**write task** — one asyncio task of the run's task group performing one entity's store write: the gate of §5.4, or a D11 correction of an entity already written; the queue loop cannot exit while one is outstanding." I refuse the `tasks_running` alternative: in this file "task" already means the `AgentTask`, so `task.tasks_running` would give one word two meanings — the same rule broken from the other side. The objection that from step 5 a gate prefilters and judges before it writes is answered by the glossary row, which defines a write task as a task that ENDS in a store write; that is exactly why the loop must wait for it.

**2. Is the ordering argument sound, and is the last-submitted text guaranteed on disk?**

The argument is sound and I measured both halves: `create_task` schedules the first step through `loop.call_soon`, whose ready queue is FIFO, so five tasks created in a row ran in creation order [0,1,2,3,4]; and awaiting a coroutine that contains no `await` runs it to completion inside that first step, so an awaitless write task never interleaves with another.

But the plan must not rest on it, because the property you actually want has a stronger and simpler warrant. `on_answer` assigns `self.results[idx] = text` BEFORE it starts the write task, and `_correct` reads `task.results[idx]` inside the coroutine body, at write time. So every pending correction task writes the newest text: last-submitted-wins holds even if the tasks ran in reverse order, interleaved, or if one were dropped. The FIFO argument, by contrast, expires the moment a write acquires an `await` — and it plausibly will, since the correction is a blocking LMDB write plus `invalidate_vectors` across every vector store, and moving it to a thread is the obvious future step. So write the invariant, not the ordering: "a write task reads `task.results[idx]` when it writes, never a text captured when it was started." Two corrections of one entity then produce two identical `update_interpretation` calls, each invalidating that entity's vectors — wasted work, not a defect; do not add a coalescing flag.

The interaction with the entity's own gate needs no ordering argument either: the `_DONE` branch is reachable only after `_write` has set `state[idx] = _DONE` at the end of its own synchronous body, and the `_GATING` branch covers the whole window before that. And a gate whose `_write` raised leaves the state at `_GATING`, so a later correction of it replaces the text and starts nothing — correct, since the run is failing anyway.

**3. Does dropping `GateError` lose anything steps 4–8 rely on?**

Nothing that is matched by class — I verified the whole tree: production has only the definition (semantic_interpretation.py:849) and the raise (:903); no `except GateError` exists anywhere in the package. The class matches are §15.5's plan block and two tests. And `add_note` genuinely reaches the user: `traceback.format_exception` renders `__notes__` on the line after the message (measured), rpc.py:344-347 forwards that whole string, and `extract_user_error` finds no marker in it, so `interpretation_rpc_error` prints the entire traceback with the note and the entity's name in it — strictly more than `GateError`'s one line. So the decision is right. Four consequences must be handled:

(a) §15.5's `_gate` carries `except GateError: raise` (vacuous — that try has no `except Exception` arm) and, three lines below, the second `gate_finished()` that hangs the run. Both go; the try disappears entirely (item 2).

(b) The note text must belong to the write site, not to the gate: §5.4 puts step 6's failure on the same channel, and step 6 writes a DEPENDENT's gate fields. One baked sentence would name the wrong entity, and the note is now the only carrier of that identity (item 7).

(c) The entity name leaves `str(exc)`, so archive/tests/test_interpretation_driver.py:275-276 must assert against the formatted traceback instead, and §10's and §15.10's "`GateError` fails the run" must be reworded to name the property.

(d) The real loss is a type-level guarantee: with a class nobody caught, no `except Exception` in the gate could ever eat a store failure. Steps 4–5 add two such arms (`_prefilter`'s and `_judge`'s). Do NOT reintroduce the class for this; write the rule in §5.4 instead, and write it accurately — the plan's own `_judge` DOES enclose a store write (the driver's per-turn `write_cost` flush), and that is acceptable because a swallowed judge failure resolves CHANGED, which is D2's conservative answer, and the same broken store fails the gate's own write moments later. Add the companion rule too: never `add_note` an exception whose message carries `USER_ERROR_MARKER` — notes render after the message and `extract_user_error` returns everything after the marker to the end of the string, so the note would be shown to the user as part of the error text.

**4. Does `raise leaves[0] from leaves[0].__cause__` ever worsen what Isabelle shows?**

Yes — and after this change it is the normal case, not a corner. Re-raising a leaf inside `except ExceptionGroup` overwrites that leaf's `__context__` with the group, and `from leaves[0].__cause__` — which is `from None` for a native store exception — then suppresses it. So for the exception class this change is designed to surface, the form both clobbers and hides the leaf's own chain. It is a live path: `put_interpretation` → `invalidate_vectors` → `invalidate_vectors_in_store` → `_get_lmdb_env` → `_rebuild_corrupt_store`'s `os.rename` inside `except _CORRUPTION_ERRORS as e:` (semantic_embedding.py:1053-1079, documented as propagating) hands `_write` an OSError whose `__cause__` is None and whose `__context__` is the corruption error — the lead the operator needs. Measured side by side: raising inside the handler prints only the OSError and its note; raising after the except block has been left prints "ValueError: lmdb: store is corrupt / During handling of the above exception… / OSError: ENOSPC… / while writing the interpretation of T.foo", with no group and no `    | ` gutter anywhere. So the answer is not "correct the `from` clause" but "stop raising inside the handler": the group is then dropped structurally, because nothing is being handled at the raise site, and no `from` and no `__suppress_context__` mutation is needed at all. I also confirmed the marked case is unaffected: a `FatalAgentError` leaf carrying `USER_ERROR_MARKER` still yields exactly its own message through `extract_user_error` under the new shape.

**5. Should `_unwrap_gate_failures` keep its `CancelledError` filter?**

Yes, unchanged — F11's rejection stands and nothing here reopens it. I re-verified the mechanism rather than taking it on trust: `TaskGroup.__aexit__` raises `self._base_error` bare before it ever constructs a group, so a child raising `KeyboardInterrupt` alongside a child raising `ValueError` reaches the caller as a bare `KeyboardInterrupt` with `isinstance(e, BaseExceptionGroup)` False — it never matches `except ExceptionGroup` and never reaches the helper. D10's "a group carrying SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt propagates untouched" is therefore honoured by asyncio for free, which makes the filter dead code today; but deleting it would edit an approved §5.4 sentence to remove two lines of cheap defence and the only test of a plan-mandated clause. Under the raise-outside shape the "nothing but cancellations" branch becomes "return `eg` unchanged" and the caller's single `raise failure` re-raises the group, so `test_unwrapping_takes_the_first_failure_and_ignores_cancellations` keeps both assertions with no change beyond the call shape.
